newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares up on large deals in three firms.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares up on large deals in three firms.

text.p: Jordan's stock market was underpinned on Tuesday by large deals in two leading industrial shares and Arab Bank, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.73 percent to 154.90 points in turnover of 472,602 dinars ($667,542).
It was the highest rise in the AMF index since the start of the traditionally quiet Moslem fasting month of Ramadan three weeks ago.
"There was demand on the solid stocks which were mostly large bloc deals. Aside from that the remaining stock had weak demand," one broker said.
He predicted that the market would pick up after a law relating to the distributing of bonus shares has been passed. The law is currently being debated in parliament.
Many banks and leading companies plan to benefit from the proposed elimination of a 15 percent tax on capitalisation which the new law is to introduce.
The busiest stock of the day was Jordan Cement Factories which rose 0.01 dinars in healthy turnover of 93,560 dinars attributed to a large deal by an institutional investor.
The other heavily traded stock, Jordan Phosphate Mines, was unchanged at 3.40 dinars in trade worth 73,975 dinars.
Another busy stock was Arab Bank, which rose 2.50 dinars in trade worth 41,000 dinars.
Rising shares outnumbered fallers by 20 to five, with another 10 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange rose 0.29 percent to 81.81 points.
